messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: Unidentified

Date of Admission: Not specified

Date of Discharge: Not specified

Reason for Admission: Pain in right shoulder and left thigh with prior history of moderate trauma

Summary:

A 14-year-old male of Afghan descent was admitted to the hospital with pain in his right shoulder and left thigh following a history of moderate trauma. Physical examination revealed fever, elevated leukocyte count, mild polymorphonuclear predominance, and reduced range of motion in the right shoulder. X-ray imaging showed mixed density, periosteal reaction, and cortical disruption with soft tissue swelling in the metaphysis of the right humerus and left fibula. Computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging detected two lesions involving the bone marrow and cortex in the head of the humerus and body of the fibula. A biopsy of the proximal humerus revealed diffuse inflammatory infiltration, consistent with xanthogranulomatous osteomyelitis. Deep fluid samples also showed Staphylococcus aureus infection, sensitive to cloxacillin, which was administered to the patient. After hospitalization, the patient's general condition improved, and he was able to walk without pain. The patient left the hospital without completing the duration of treatment, but did not report any relapse of pain or discharge at his follow-up appointment within 4 months in an outpatient clinical setting.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Condition at Discharge: Improved

Treatment: Cloxacillin

Follow-up Care: Follow-up appointment within 4 months in an outpatient clinical setting

Prognosis: Good

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
1. The condition chiefly responsible for the admission is Staphylococcus aureus osteomyelitis (xanthogranulomatous type) affecting both the right humerus and the left fibula, confirmed on biopsy and deep fluid culture.
2. Osteomyelitis is a disease of the musculoskeletal system, which is chapter M.
3. Osteomyelitis falls under category M86, with the organism coded separately as a secondary code.

CODE: M86
